decision.notes: Everything else in the attempt is fine (sections, table, links). Keep it and fix only the measurement script.
reasons: The measurement script in docs/runbooks/knowledge.md ends input to the MCP server after a fixed `sleep 5`. That is timing-dependent: on a slower machine the server is cut off before it answers every get_context, the script prints a partial table, and the rule that every runbook command runs as written breaks. Replace the sleep with deterministic completion. For example, a small node script spawns `out/main/mcp.js`, sends each request, waits for the response with the matching id, and closes stdin only after the last one arrives. Re-run it as written and update the recorded outputs if they change.

content.summary: Sprint 1 delivered the whole Knowledge layers epic. The orchestrator now runs from an 800-word kernel (skills/orchestrator.md, 798 words, down from 5,513) plus 44 built-in facts. The facts are pushed as a `context` field by state-changing orchestrator commands and pulled with the new get_context command, within a token budget. Facts load from built-in, overall (a per-machine git repo) and repo layers with repo > overall > built-in precedence, and the desktop Knowledge card registers the overall repository and shows layer status. The runbook records about 8,515 tokens for the old guide against 1,313 for the kernel plus 249-1,371 per pushed event. All 8 work tickets and the acceptance node were accepted; DM-477 needed a second attempt. The acceptance round found and fixed integration problems: deadcode drift, two outdated tests, pre-existing git-stash test timeouts (fixed with the person's approval), and branch coverage below the threshold. The Definition of Done then passed on the combined work, landed as one squashed commit e449a65 on knowledge-layers.
